learning_objective: 🎯 Discover how Indian culture reacted to British influence through social reform, and understand concepts like Sanskritisation and Westernisation!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Thinkers like Raja Rammohun Roy and Sir Syed Ahmed Khan used modern Western ideas (democracy, reason) combined with ancient texts to fight against practices like Sati, child marriage, and caste discrimination.
A concept by M.N. Srinivas. It is the process where lower castes try to move up the social ladder by adopting the customs, rituals, and vegetarian diets of the 'twice-born' upper castes.
The changes brought about in Indian society and culture (technology, institutions, ideology, values) due to 150 years of British rule. This affected diet, clothing, and education.
Moving towards a rational, scientific outlook (Modernisation) and the decline in the everyday influence of religion, making way for equality and reason (Secularisation).

fun_activity.title: 👔 Wardrobe Check
fun_activity.instructions: Open your closet. Count how many clothes are traditional Indian wear versus Western wear (jeans, t-shirts, shirts). This ratio is a direct visual example of 'Westernisation' in daily life!

exam_tips: 📌 Always credit M.N. Srinivas when writing about Sanskritisation and Westernisation.
📌 Note that Sanskritisation is not always positive; it often leads to stricter rules for women (like ending widow remarriage) in lower castes trying to emulate upper castes.
📌 Modernisation in India didn't destroy tradition; rather, traditions adapted (e.g., using the internet to broadcast religious pujas).
quick_recap: ⭐ The printing press played a massive role in spreading reformist ideas across India.
⭐ Westernisation created a new English-educated middle class in India.
⭐ Both Sanskritisation and Westernisation occurred simultaneously in different parts of Indian society.
